By using FactorEscalaTop v2.4, you formally accept the following terms and conditions:

 Cartographic & Geodetic Scope: The application is calibrated for reference systems in the Plurinational State of Bolivia (UTM Zones 19S & 20S, WGS84, and Lambert Conformal Conic Projection).

 Engineering Suite & Surveying Tools: Includes IGM Factor Calculation (k, ha, K), Vincenty Geodesic Algorithms (Direct & Inverse), Slope Distance Reduction, UTM Line Geometry, Lambert Conversion, Offline Mapping, and Stakeout with GIS/CAD import & export (KML, CSV, DXF 3D, GPX, GeoJSON).

 Geoid Models & Elevation: Integrates official MGBol08 (EGM2008) and global EGM96 geoid models, as well as online MSL orthometric elevation retrieval via Copernicus DEM GLO-90.

 Weather Assistant & Sensors: Drone weather analysis and altimetry rely on local sensors (barometer, compass, GPS) and external APIs. Core calculation tools operate 100% offline.

 Technical Support Character: Results provided are technical support tools for engineers and surveyors. It is the professional's sole responsibility to verify, validate, and certify calculations before formal project application.

 Regulatory Compliance: The user agrees to use the tool in compliance with applicable technical standards and regulations in Bolivia.

In compliance with Google Play guidelines for data protection, this policy details how information is managed:

 Location Usage (GPS): The application processes real-time geolocation data to execute geodetic calculations and project maps. Data is processed locally and may be used in the background to maintain session pin persistence.

 Local Storage and Export: Points and records are stored exclusively in the device's internal memory. Exported files (TXT/JSON) are the user's responsibility.

 Third-Party Services: We use Google Play Services for maps, Open-Meteo API for weather and elevation data, and ArcGIS (Esri) for satellite layers.

 Security: No personal data is collected or sold to external developer servers.

FactorEscalaTop v2.4 is a professional topographic workstation aimed at surveyors, civil engineers, and geomatics professionals in Bolivia.

What can you do?
 • IGM Factors: Calculate scale, elevation, and combined factors with 9 decimals.
 • GNSS Pro: Stabilize and filter GNSS data in real time.
 • Stakeout & GIS: Navigate to points and import/export in KML, CSV, DXF, GeoJSON, and GPX.
 • Field Tools: Analyze drone weather, use offline maps (1GB), pro compass, and digital notebook.

AVAILABLE FUNCTIONS:

 • SEARCH (Top Panel): Tap to search and navigate to specific coordinates (Lat/Lon).
 • BROOM (Orange): Clears visual measurements and temporary polygons from the map.
 • POLYGON/RULER (Blue): Activates area and distance measurement tools. Use the MARK button to fix vertices on the orange crosshair.
 • PIN (Light Blue): Opens the dialog to save the central point to your records database.
 • LIST (Green): Allows selecting and viewing multiple saved points on the map.
 • MAP (White): Instantly toggles between Street (OSM) and Satellite (Esri) layers.

GEODESIC CALCULATIONS:
 This tool solves the fundamental problems of geodesy on the WGS84 ellipsoid using Vincenty's algorithms.

 • DIRECT: Allows finding the coordinates of a destination point from an initial point, an azimuth, and a distance.
 • INVERSE: Calculates the geodesic distance and azimuths between two known coordinates.

 Ideal for calculating long baselines where Earth's curvature is significant.

DISTANCE REDUCTION:
 Allows transforming a distance measured on the ground (Slope) to its equivalent value on the reference ellipsoid.

 PROCESS:
 1. Horizontal Reduction: Eliminates the effect of the elevation difference between points A and B.
 2. Ellipsoidal Reduction: Projects the horizontal distance to the ellipsoid surface considering the mean height.

 Essential for linking Total Station measurements with GNSS geodetic networks.

UTM LINE CALCULATOR:
 Calculates geometric parameters between two coordinates projected in the UTM system.

 • Grid Distance: Direct distance on the cartographic grid.
 • Grid Azimuth: Angle relative to Grid North.
 • Meridian Convergence: Angular difference between Geographic North and Grid North at each point.

 Useful for civil engineering and urban cadastre projects.

BOLIVIA LAMBERT PROJECTION:
 Specialized converter for the LCC (Lambert Conformal Conic) projection, officially used in Bolivia for regional scale mapping.

 Allows bidirectional transformation between geographic coordinates (Lat/Lon) and Lambert plane coordinates (X, Y) maintaining angle conformity.

 Configured with standard parameters for the Bolivian territory.

MANUAL DATA ENTRY:
 Module designed for processing individual coordinates entered via keyboard.

 • UTM Projection: Enter metric coordinates (E, N), zone, and hemisphere to obtain correction factors.
 • Geodesic: Enter Latitude and Longitude in decimal format.

 The system will automatically apply the geoid model selected in settings for height and pressure calculations.

DIGITAL FIELD NOTEBOOK:
 Optimizes the recording of topographic radiation directly from the mobile.

 REQUIRED DATA:
 • Station: Identification and instrument height.
 • Reference: Sighted point for orientation.
 • Radiation: ID of the auxiliary point and its metric coordinates.

 Data is securely saved in the local database and can be exported from the RECORDS tab.

PROFESSIONAL COMPASS AND LEVEL:
 Support tool for orientation and sensor leveling.

 • Azimuth: Real-time reading of the angle relative to Geographic North.
 • Bubble Level: Visual indicator to ensure device horizontality (Crucial for GNSS precision).
 • Technical Panel: Displays current location and GPS-synchronized UTM coordinates.

1. DATA IMPORT (.txt):
 Each line of the file must follow this exact comma-separated format:
 Name, EastE, NorthN, UTM, Zone, Hemisphere
 Ex: P01, 816663.123E, 8088744.094N, UTM, 19, S

 2. STATIC MODE SWITCH (Target Icon):
 This button controls the advanced GNSS Processing Layer.

 • 🔴 RED (Dynamic Mode): Use while walking towards the point. GPS responds instantly to your movement.

 • 🟢 GREEN (Precision Filter): Use upon reaching the stakeout point. The system averages the position to eliminate noise and fix the exact distance.

 3. RECOMMENDED FIELD PROTOCOL:
 1. Approach the point following the arrow in RED mode.
 2. When less than 1 meter away, stop and switch to GREEN mode.
 3. Keep the equipment motionless for 15 to 20 seconds.
 4. The distance will stabilize. Mark the ground with full confidence.
